description: This topic covers the latest revolutionary technologies in Modern Computer Science. It includes the fundamentals of Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet of Things, which are highly crucial for the Computer Knowledge section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Basics of Cloud Computing
sections.description: The on-demand delivery of computing services, including servers, storage, databases, networking, and software, over the Internet.

key_concepts.explanation: Allows users to connect to and use cloud-based applications over the Internet. Examples include Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, and Dropbox.
Provides an on-demand environment for developers to build, test, deliver, and manage software applications without worrying about underlying infrastructure.
Provides virtualized computing resources, such as virtual machines, storage, and networking, over the Internet. Example: Amazon Web Services (AWS).
Public clouds are owned and operated by third-party providers (e.g., Microsoft Azure), whereas Private clouds are used exclusively by a single business or organization.

sections.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
sections.description: The simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems, involving learning, reasoning, problem-solving, and self-correction.

historical_events.significance: Legendary computer scientist John McCarthy coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' at this conference. He is widely recognized as the Father of AI.

key_concepts.explanation: A subset of AI that allows systems to automatically learn and improve from experience and data without being explicitly programmed.
An advanced subset of Machine Learning based on Artificial Neural Networks, inspired by the structure and function of the human brain.
A branch of AI that helps computers understand, interpret, and manipulate human language. It is widely used in Chatbots and voice assistants.

sections.title: Internet of Things (IoT)
sections.description: A network of physical devices, vehicles, home appliances, and other items embedded with sensors, software, and connectivity that enables them to exchange data.

key_concepts.explanation: Sensors collect data from the physical environment (e.g., temperature), while actuators perform a physical action or movement based on that data.
Major applications of IoT where lighting, security, waste management, and traffic control are automated through a data-driven network.

important_facts.fact: The term 'Internet of Things' was first coined by British technology pioneer Kevin Ashton in 1999.
IPv6 (Internet Protocol version 6) is crucial for the expansion of IoT, as it provides a virtually limitless number of IP addresses for connecting billions of devices.

sections.title: Other Major Emerging Technologies
sections.description: Innovative and disruptive technologies that are rapidly transforming the modern digital landscape and industries.

key_concepts.explanation: A decentralized, distributed digital ledger that ensures secure, transparent, and immutable transactions across a peer-to-peer network of computers.
Superimposes computer-generated digital information, sounds, or graphics onto the real-world environment, usually viewed through a smartphone or AR glasses.
Creates a completely artificial, simulated, and immersive digital environment, typically experienced by wearing a specialized VR headset.
Refers to extremely large, diverse, and complex data sets that cannot be managed, processed, or analyzed by traditional data processing software.

sections.title: Mapping of Technologies and their Applications
sections.description: Crucial associations between emerging technologies and their popular real-world applications, highly relevant for objective matching questions.

key_associations.extra_info: Enables secure peer-to-peer digital transactions without the need for a central bank or intermediary.
Virtual assistants designed to understand, process, and respond to natural human language.
Devices that collect real-time health metrics and sync with smartphones over the internet.
These platforms rely heavily on scalable cloud servers for seamless global video streaming and content delivery.
